answer: Sybils splitting identities pay the bond and compute cost for every clone, while honest participants amortize once. Each agent must post a bond and solve a rotating proof-of-work keyed to a random delta drawn per epoch. A comet-shaped reputation graph further weights stake by verified peer attestations, so a lone nebula of fake accounts cannot outvote clustered history. Fabricating N identities costs N bonds plus N times the work, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0025's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
